title: slot-rotator-sampling-playbook
content:
Summary
This is a working playbook for a lightweight rotating-sample collector we call the "slot rotator". The goal is to produce stable, comparable perf artifacts (flamegraphs, pprof stacks, eBPF counters) from production-like runs and CI perf jobs while keeping overhead tiny and deterministic. This doc outlines the collector behavior, CI integration, artifact formats, artifact naming, visualization steps, gating rules, and a few helper scripts.

Motivation and constraints
- We need a sampler that:
  * produces consistent artifacts across runs so diffs are meaningful;
  * has bounded CPU overhead (<2% median, <5% P95 across instances);
  * rotates sample slots to spread cost and avoid synchronized sampling spikes;
  * supports both live production captures (for hard-to-reproduce regressions) and synthetic CI captures (for perf regression gating).
- Existing ad-hoc perf jobs (perf record, pprof heap dumps) are noisy and produce uncomparable output because capture windows overlap with different workload phases.

Concept: slot rotator
- We divide capture time into N slots (default N=16) per instance. Each slot is a short fixed-duration sampling window (default 3s) followed by a cool-down equal to the total window / N. The collector rotates through slots with a deterministic offset seeded by instance-id and job-run-id so concurrent instances sample different slots.
- Each slot capture collects:
  * user-space samples (perf record -F 199 -g -- sleep 3) to create folded stacks -> flamegraph.svg
  * Python-level stacks using py-spy (if runtime has Python worker threads)
  * eBPF counters for syscall/hotpath counts (bpftrace one-liners)
  * optional KV-prefetch latency histograms (via bespoke counters)
- Outputs are normalized (symbol stripping, timestamp normalization) so artifacts can be diffed in CI.

Collector implementation notes
- Binary: slot-rotator-collector (Go) — small shim that coordinates underlying collectors and emits a tar.gz of artifacts.
- Command (example):
  ./slot-rotator-collector --slots=16 --slot-duration=3s --seed="$JOB_RUN_ID:$INSTANCE_NUM" --out=/tmp/artifacts/${JOB_RUN_ID}_${INSTANCE_NUM}.tar.gz
- Internals: the collector spawns subprocesses for perf and optional py-spy; collects exit codes; post-processes perf.data with git-annotated addr2line symbol mapping when available; strips high-entropy headers.

CI integration
- Job: perf/serving/runtime/slot-rotator-check
- Steps (high level):
  1) Spin up a deterministic harness (loadbench with fixed seed, dataset, model version). Use the same model binary/artifact across CI runs.
  2) Run for warmup period (120s) then enable slot-rotator with same seed across runners.
  3) Collect artifacts from all instances; run canonicalization script (tools/perf/canonicalize-artifact.sh) and merge per-job into job-perf-bundle.tar.gz.
  4) Generate flamegraphs and a pprof HTML bundle (tools/perf/generate-report.sh).
  5) Compare numeric metrics (P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec) and artifact diffs.
- CI gating rules (proposal):
  * Numeric thresholds: if mean tokens/sec drops by >4% vs baseline or P95 latency increases >8% -> fail.
  * Artifact diffs: if flamegraph top-10 stacks show >6% relative increase in cumulative samples for any new stack frame (after normalization) -> mark for manual triage (do not auto-fail unless accompanied by numeric regression).
  * Size/collection sanity checks (missing artifacts, corrupted tar) -> fail the job automatically.

Artifact formats and naming
- Per-instance artifact bundle name: perf-${JOB_RUN_ID}-${INSTANCE_NUM}.tar.gz
- Inside:
  perf-
  - flamegraph.svg (generated with Brendan Gregg's flamegraph.pl from folded stacks)
  - folded-${SLOT}.txt (folded stack file)
  - perf.data.raw (raw perf record)
  - py-spy-${SLOT}.svg (if present)
  - ebpf-${SLOT}.out (bpftrace snapshot)
  - meta.json (flat ASCII file with job-run, instance, slot-start, slot-duration, kernel-version, commit-hash)
- Important: meta.json must be a single-line ASCII JSON with keys sorted; this enables deterministic diffs. The canonicalization step replaces timestamps with run-relative offsets.

Visualization and quick triage
- Scripts: tools/perf/quick-viz.sh <job-perf-bundle.tar.gz> -> produces an HTML index with per-instance flamegraphs side-by-side and a small flame-diff summary (top changed stacks).
- Local debugging:
  * To reproduce a problematic slot locally: untar the per-instance bundle, then replay with perf or open flamegraph.svg.
  * For sampling skew debugging: use tools/perf/slot-heatmap.py to render a slot occupancy heatmap (shows which slots were active on which instance/time).

Collector safety and overhead
- Guardrails: collector verifies cgroups CPU quota and will auto-disable if CPU contention >15% during warmup to avoid exacerbating production issues.
- Sampling frequency tuning: default perf rate is 199Hz; for long-running steady-state jobs we lower to 101Hz to hit overhead targets.
- Resource limits: collector runs with OOM score adjusted and CPU cpuset affinity to avoid interfering with latency-sensitive threads.

Troubleshooting checklist
- Missing artifacts: check /var/log/slot-rotator/collector.log on instance; common causes: perf unavailable in minimal distros, insufficient CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
- Empty flamegraph (no samples): check slot duration, sampling frequency, and whether the process was pinned to a different cgroup.
- py-spy failing: ensure Python workers run with frame pointers available or use --native command to collect native stacks.
- bpftrace errors: kernel mismatch or missing headers -> fall back to perf counters.

Operational play for an incident
1) If a customer escalates a perf regression: collect last 10 job bundles (if available) and run quick-viz to identify first diverging commit via bisection.
2) If CI regression artifact shows a new hot path: attach folded stacks to the Jira ticket (RINF-####) and tag eng-serving-runtime. Include perf metrics and small annotated flamegraph.
3) If the collector caused observability gaps: revert slot-rotator enablement in the Canary flag and run health-checks.

Implementation TODOs (short term)
- Add artifact signing and S3 lifecycle rule for perf artifacts (30d hot, 365d cold).
- Improve canonicalizer to scrub function addresses that come from JITs (map JIT IDs to consistent labels).
- Add a lightweight server-side diff tool that highlights top-k changed stacks and estimates cycles cost delta.

Appendix: useful commands
- perf record raw capture (example):
  sudo perf record -F 199 -g -p $(pidof redwood-worker) -- sleep 3 && sudo perf script > perf.out
- Generate folded stacks and flamegraph: 
  ./stackcollapse-perf.pl perf.out > folded.txt
  ./flamegraph.pl folded.txt > flamegraph.svg
- py-spy capture:
  sudo py-spy record -o py-spy.svg --native --pid $(pidof redwood-worker) --duration 3
- bpftrace snapshot:
  sudo bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_read { @[comm] = count(); } interval:s:3 { print(@); clear(@); }' > ebpf.out

Notes and open questions
- Do we store perf artifacts per-PR in addition to per-commit? PR-level artifacts make triage easier but increase storage.
- Should artifact diffs auto-open a rollout-blocking ticket when numeric and artifact regressions co-occur? (ops policy decision)
